title: The Incredible story of the escape
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：incredible　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 incredible 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the observer wrote of ① an incredible story of the escape in the log, and everybody in the observatory said at once that it was ② more incredible than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the observer, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the incredible ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most incredible story of the escape anybody in the observatory had ever seen, or so the log for November 1965 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too incredible to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the incredible ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lens at the far dome, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an incredible view from the ridge, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as incredible as the view from the ridge they had once had in the old observatory. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was incredible or not, and he said so.

By 1978 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something incredible, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next observatory called the whole plan ⑧ quite incredible; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the incredible ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1981, with great care, she wrote of another incredible story of the escape in the same log, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ more incredible than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most incredible view from the ridge in the whole observatory, she said in 1983, was the one she could never quite name; the incredible ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 难以置信（前置定语 an incredible story of the escape：1971 年观测员在观测记录里记下的那件难以置信的离奇经过）
B. adj. 难以置信／极好（比较级 more incredible than：文中两处，一处比脱险的离奇经过，一处比预想）
C. adj. 难以置信／极好（最高级 the most incredible：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 难以置信（表语 too incredible to do：母亲觉得它太难以置信，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 极好（前置定语 an incredible view from the ridge：叔叔把整件事称作一桩极好的景致）
F. adj. 极好（同级比较 as incredible as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩山脊上令人难以置信的景致相比）
G. adj. 极好（后置定语 something incredible：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 极好（受程度副词修饰 quite incredible：那位助手的评价）

items.q: an incredible story of the escape
the most incredible story of the escape anybody
an incredible view from the ridge
The most incredible view from the ridge in

answers.why: incredible 意为“难以置信”，1971 年观测员在观测记录里记下的是“一件难以置信的离奇经过”，此处作前置定语 an incredible story of the escape。
incredible 意为“难以置信”，此处用比较级 more incredible than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
incredible 意为“难以置信”，观测记录上 十一月 那行字说它是观测站里最难以置信的一件，故用最高级 the most incredible story of the escape。
incredible 意为“难以置信”，母亲认为这件东西“太难以置信了，谁也用不上”，too incredible to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
incredible 意为“极好”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩极好的景致”，此处作前置定语 an incredible view from the ridge。
incredible 意为“极好”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩山脊上令人难以置信的景致一样极好”，同级比较用 as incredible as。
incredible 意为“极好”，观测记录上那半行字要的是“极好的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something incredible。
incredible 意为“极好”，邻观测站来的那位助手认为这套计划“相当极好”，quite 修饰原级 incredible。
incredible 意为“极好”，1981 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要极好”，故用比较级 more incredible than。
incredible 意为“极好”，母亲 1983 年说的是“整个观测站里最极好的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most incredible view from the ridge。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，观测员在观测记录里记下了一件难以置信的离奇经过。（an incredible story of the escape）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更难以置信。（more incredible than …）
母亲觉得它太难以置信，谁也用不上。（too incredible to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩极好的景致。（an incredible view from the ridge）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩山脊上令人难以置信的景致一样极好。（as incredible as …）
到了 1978 年，观测记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件极好的东西。（something incredible）
answers: In 1971 the observer wrote of an incredible story of the escape in the log.
Everybody said it was more incredible than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too incredible to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an incredible view from the ridge.
He said nobody would call it as incredible as the view from the ridge they had once had.
By 1978 the log asked for nothing but something incredible.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 incredible 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the observer wrote of an incredible story of the escape in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most incredible story of the escape in the observatory, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too incredible to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an incredible view from the ridge, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next observatory called the plan quite incredible, and everybody laughed.
The incredible ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
